title: Ray.so — export code snippets as good-looking images
desc: No more screenshotting when you share code. Colours and window padding are adjustable, and the exported PNG drops straight into an article.

title: Warp — a modern terminal with block output
desc: Commands and their output are split into collapsible blocks, so scrolling back through history stops being a fight. Completions are smarter than a default shell too.

title: Fontshare — free fonts you can use commercially
desc: Every family ships complete weights, and the site suggests pairings up front — easier than digging through Google Fonts when you need a display face.

title: Chinese Copywriting Guidelines
desc: Clear rules for spacing between Chinese and Latin text, full- vs half-width punctuation, and number usage. Handy to cite when the team argues about whether a space belongs there.

title: CoRecursive — the stories behind the code
desc: Each episode has an author explain why they designed it that way. Better than docs for understanding the trade-offs behind a choice, and just right for a commute.

title: The Book of Shaders — fragment shaders from zero
desc: From GLSL basics to noise and pattern generation, with every example editable in the browser and live. The shortest path into graphics.

title: doocs/md — a Markdown editor for WeChat articles
desc: Markdown on the left, live layout on the right. Theme, size and code highlighting are all configurable, and one copy pastes into the WeChat editor without breaking styles.

title: PowerToys — Microsoft's own Windows power pack
desc: FancyZones for custom tiling, PowerRename for bulk renames, a colour picker, Alt+Space quick launch. One install replaces a pile of little utilities.

title: Files — a modern Windows file manager
desc: Tabs, dual-pane copying, cloud sync badges. What Explorer should have grown into — the open-source community built it for Microsoft.

title: LocalSend — cross-platform transfers over your LAN
desc: Move files between phone and laptop with no server and no cable. Clients on every platform: an open-source AirDrop that works everywhere.

title: Excalidraw — a hand-drawn whiteboard
desc: Architecture diagrams and rough flows come out relaxed; nothing has to be pixel-aligned to look right. Share a link for live collaboration, and the SVG export is clean.

title: IT Tools — a developer's utility drawer
desc: Timestamps, JWT decoding, regex testing, Base64, UUIDs… a hundred-odd everyday tools on one page, and you can self-host a copy.

title: Upscayl — open-source AI image upscaling
desc: One click to super-resolve old photos and blurry images. The model runs locally with no uploads, and a modest GPU is enough. It has rescued several assets for me.

title: PicGo — an image-host uploader
desc: Drag a screenshot in and it uploads to GitHub / Qiniu / SM.MS, leaving a Markdown image link on your clipboard. Zero friction when illustrating a post.

title: Motrix — a clean all-purpose downloader
desc: HTTP, BitTorrent and magnet links in one client. The interface is tidy, with no ads or bundled extras, and the download list is pleasant to look at.

title: Penpot — open-source design collaboration
desc: A Figma alternative in the browser. Your design data stays yours and can be self-hosted, and output is SVG/CSS — unusually friendly to developers.
